strategyReview: The engine's top performer remains weekend Hyperliquid funding reversion long, with 70% win rate across 363 live trades and strong shadow outcomes, though open positions show minor unrealized losses. Polymarket one-touch NO edge signals produced excellent live returns but recent shadow tests reveal a cluster of compression losses when the sell‑YES edge shrinks during bullish spot runs. The informed‑flow asymmetry and GOLD PC‑ratio extreme low discoveries are statistically robust and should be promoted to shadow tests. Several counter‑trend setups (gold cap‑edge shorts, CBRS extreme funding longs, BTC IV compression) are failing because their core assumptions — that extreme mispricing or funding extremes guarantee mean reversion — are invalidated in real regimes; they need trend‑context filters or retirement.

failureClusters.theme: One‑touch NO edge compression during rallies
failureClusters.evidence: 5 of the last 8 resolved ONE_TOUCH_HIGH_EDGE_NO shadows lost with reason `thesis_compressed_loss`; spillover to BTC and ETH contracts where edge narrowed as spot rose, closing at a loss.
failureClusters.recommendation: Tighten the shadow exit rule: exit when the sell‑YES edge drops by ≥ 1.5 pts from entry, not only when it disappears entirely. This limits drawdowns from early edge shrinkage.

failureClusters.theme: Extreme funding reversion signals failing in weak‑trend assets
failureClusters.evidence: CBRS and AAPL shadow tests show funding can persist deeply negative or worsen further, especially outside true weekends, causing losses. H‑539 (CBRS) lost 8 of 18 recent tests; H‑537 (AAPL) lost 8 of 15.
failureClusters.recommendation: Add a funding ‘bounce’ filter (off the 24h low) and require the spot to be oversold (below 7d SMA) before entering, so the trade only fires when pressure is already starting to ease.

newHypotheses.description: Fade dumb‑money highs on upside one‑touch contracts. When tracked smart wallets are net short YES (smart_flow_stance ≤ -1) on above‑strike contracts, sell YES (short) because the crowd is overpaying for upside protection.
GOLD put/call ratio extreme low short, ignoring positive trend. When GOLD's GLD put/call ratio falls into the bottom 10% of its 7‑day range (extreme call buying), short the spot.
Rich PM IV NO fade on upside touch. When Polymarket IV exceeds listed‑option IV by ≥ 10 vol points on any asset's above‑strike one‑touch contracts, sell YES (short).
BTC one‑touch NO edge with moderate strength. On BTC above‑strike contracts only, sell YES when the sell‑YES edge is between 3 and 8 pts.
Rich PM IV NO fade near expiry. Combine rich PM IV (≥10 vol pts above options) with contracts expiring within 30 days on upside touch contracts.
GOLD one‑touch NO edge near expiry. On GOLD above‑strike contracts expiring within 30 days, sell YES when the edge is ≥ 1 pt.
OIL one‑touch NO edge with tight edge band. When the sell‑YES edge on OIL upside one‑touch contracts is between 1 and 3 pts, sell YES (short).
Refinement of H‑534: Add a bearish trend filter. Only take the gold cap‑edge short when spot is below its 24h SMA, avoiding strong uptrends where high cap‑edge reflects genuine bullish demand.

Refinement of H‑539: Require funding to have already bounced off its 24h low and be in the bottom 5% of the 30d range. This avoids entries while funding is still free‑falling and only captures true reversal starts.
newHypotheses.prediction: CBRS spot moves >2% up within 2 days.

newHypotheses.description: Refinement of H‑537: Add deep extreme percentile and oversold spot filter. Only long AAPL when funding is in the bottom 5% of 30d range and the stock is below its 7d SMA, providing a reversion‑friendly context.
newHypotheses.prediction: AAPL spot moves >2% up within 2 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: All 20 shadow tests lost; the gold cap‑edge short failed because large out‑of‑the‑money call edges are driven by genuine bullish demand, not overpricing. The edge persisted and spot rallied strongly in several tests (5.37% and 3.97% up moves).
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: A large underlying‑cap edge on gold upside touch NO contracts indicates the YES price is too high and will revert, rather than reflecting durable bullish demand.

hypothesisReviews.observation: 44% win rate with many losses occurring when funding worsened further (e.g., dropping from -8.1% to -162.1%) instead of normalizing. The simple threshold fails to differentiate between temporary dislocations and persistent short pressure.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: CBRS funding < -10% reliably normalizes within 2 days without additional confirmation that the funding is already starting to revert.

hypothesisReviews.observation: The cross‑asset IV compression pattern using HYPE as risk‑on proxy produced 40% win rate. Most losses came when HYPE failed to confirm BTC strength, revealing that HYPE spot/OI is not a dependable leading indicator for BTC continuation.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: HYPE spot above SMA and stable OI confirms a >2% BTC long move over 3‑7 days.

hypothesisReviews.observation: AAPL extreme negative funding shadow tests achieved 47% win rate. Losses were concentrated when funding failed to bounce on weekday sessions even after weekend filters were applied, showing that extreme negative funding alone does not guarantee a quick snapback.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Extreme negative AAPL funding (< -10%) rapidly normalizes and leads to a >2% spot gain without requiring explicit funding recovery signals or spot oversold conditions.

hypothesisReviews.observation: BTC PM‑IV expansion reversion lost 7 of 10 recent tests, with spot moves frequently failing to reach 2% absolute. The IV spread proved to be a weak volatility predictor in calm markets, and multiple refinements that tightened thresholds did not rescue it.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: BTC PM IV below 46 while options IV remains high guarantees a >2% absolute spot move within 3 days regardless of trend context.

hypothesisReviews.observation: Listed‑IV momentum confirmation lost 7 of 10 recent tests, as rising option‑implied demand did not prevent trend reversals. Spot failed to sustain upside when macro or positioning shifted, invalidating the confirmation thesis.
hypothesisReviews.invalidatedAssumption: Spot momentum above SMA near its 7d high, combined with rising 30d opt IV change, reliably leads to further >2% spot gains over 3‑7 days.

journalEntry: Tonight’s review focused on pruning struggling counter‑trend setups that repeatedly rely on reversion assumptions which break in live testing. The gold one‑touch cap‑edge short (H‑534) failed because extreme call demand often reflects genuine bullish momentum, not mispricing — a trend filter is tentatively added. CBRS and AAPL extreme funding longs failed when funding continued to plummet; refinements require a confirmed bounce and oversold spot. The cross‑asset BTC momentum family using HYPE as confirmation is retired for now because HYPE was not a reliable leading indicator. In contrast, the informed‑flow asymmetry and GOLD PC‑ratio extreme low clusters show robust in‑sample statistics and are being promoted to shadow tests in a controlled batch. No parameter changes are warranted this cycle; live risk controls are appropriate.
